examples.problem_statement: The silent-film pioneer Harold Lloyd made a virtue of the (i) _________ limits of his day, playing men so (ii) _________ it was easy to imagine it was the character rather than the medium who lacked a voice. Blank (i): artistic / commercial / technical. Blank (ii): avant-garde / diffident / reluctant.

solution.operation: Read the closing clue "it was the character rather than the medium who lacked a voice" and ask what made the medium voiceless.
solution.result: The limits of Lloyd's day were the ones that kept sound off film - i.e. the technology of the day.
solution.description: Mine the second half of the sentence for the clue that defines blank (i): the medium, not the man, is what could not speak, so the limits in question are the ones belonging to the film technology of that era.

solution.operation: Predict a word for blank (i) - something like "technological" - and compare it against artistic, commercial, and technical.
solution.description: Commit to your own prediction before reading the options, then take the choice that matches it; "technical" is the one that carries the sense of "technological", while artistic and commercial name limits the clue never raised.

solution.operation: Ask what quality in the characters Lloyd played would explain their failure to speak, and predict a word like "mute".
solution.result: Blank (ii) needs an adjective describing a man so self-effacing he would not speak up.
solution.description: Build the prediction for blank (ii) from the same clue: the joke only works if the characters themselves seem the sort who would stay silent, so predict a word in the neighbourhood of "mute" or "shy".

solution.operation: Test diffident against that prediction: diffident means self-effacing, very shy.
solution.description: Check the meaning of diffident and confirm it delivers exactly the reticence the prediction called for - a shy, self-effacing man plausibly reads as the one lacking a voice.

solution.operation: Reject reluctant, which means unwilling in general, not "reluctant to speak"; the similar-sounding reticent is the word that means that.
solution.result: Reluctant is eliminated as a trap answer, and avant-garde never fit the clue.
solution.description: Clear the trap before finalising: reluctant is planted because it sounds like reticent, but on its own it does not carry the sense of being unwilling to speak, which is the only sense the sentence supports.

key_reminders: Predict your own word for each blank from the sentence's clues before you read the answer choices.
The contrast "the character rather than the medium" is what fixes blank (i) as a limit of the film technology.
Diffident means self-effacing or very shy; reticent - not reluctant - is the word for disinclined to speak.
common_mistakes: Choosing reluctant for blank (ii) by confusing it with the similar-sounding reticent.
Reading "limits of his day" as artistic or commercial constraints and ignoring the voice clue that makes them technical.
